h1: Apartment interior design in Los Angeles, custom furniture, and turnkey renovation, 140 m²

blocks.text: Apartment interior design in Los Angeles, custom furniture, and turnkey renovation, 140 m²

parts.html: A 140 m² apartment in Los Angeles. We did this project remotely: interior design, 3D visualization, technical documentation and the furniture design. The work covered the living room with dining area, the kitchen with built-in appliances, bedrooms, walk-in closets, entrance hall, bathrooms and storage. We also prepared a detailed cost estimate for construction and finishing work, materials, furniture, appliances, plumbing fixtures and lighting, so the scope and budget were clear before the renovation started. The gallery shows the visualizations.

blocks.text: Living room, dining area and fireplace

parts.html: The main wall of the living room is taken up entirely by light oak furniture. On the left is an open shelving unit of square cubbies, in the center a TV niche with a long bioethanol fireplace in a black frame below it, and on the right plain handleless fronts. Above the cabinets runs a row of open niches up to the ceiling, with the air-conditioning grille above them and a lit cornice along it.

The dining area with a glass table sits behind the sofa. The wall behind it is made of oak panels and insets of boldly patterned stone in gray-brown tones, and the same wall has coat hooks by the entrance. The front door is clad in oak slats. The ceiling has track systems with black spotlights and recessed downlights.

The kitchen is a galley layout. On one side are oak columns with two built-in ovens and a fridge. On the other are white handleless fronts, a white countertop, a gas cooktop and a built-in range hood. The run ends in an oak breakfast bar for two, which also separates the kitchen from the entrance hall.

The bedroom is reached through a walk-through closet with ceiling-height white wardrobes and dark vertical handles. In the bedroom itself, a countertop with drawers runs the full length of the wall opposite the bed, serving as both a desk and a dressing table. To the left above it is an oak shelving unit, to the right a backlit slat panel, and next to it a white wardrobe.

The kitchen, shelving, walk-in closets and wardrobes were designed to the dimensions of the rooms. The documentation sets out the turnkey renovation as a single sequence: construction, finishing, furniture making, fit-out.
